profiles.field_rule: Research trial: inspect the loose, drooping panicle, hairy sheaths, long lemma awns and rooted annual base together. If awns are broken or have fallen off, leave the awn question unanswered; missing projections on a damaged specimen are not an awnless trait. Large multi-flowered Bromus spikelets fit the loose-oat option, not the airy-cloud-of-tiny-spikelets button. Compare mature glume and lemma lengths with Japanese, rescue and other annual brome grasses.

profiles.field_rule: Research trial: follow the two-ranked, alternating spikelets on a single true ryegrass rachis and inspect the leaf auricles and mature lemma awns. Italian ryegrass is commonly awned but not every flowering spike has obvious awns. Distinguish it from perennial ryegrass and Lolium hybrid material using connected spikelets and leaf bases.
